challenges.title: Simple origami
challenges.description: Fold a sheet of paper (or a receipt, a flyer) into a simple shape: boat, crane, plane.
tips: Press each fold hard with your nail, the shape will hold much better.
Starting from a properly square sheet avoids half the problems.
The boat and the plane are the easiest ones to start with.

challenges.title: Recycled bookmark
challenges.description: Make a bookmark out of paper or cardboard you were about to throw away.
tips: A strip of roughly 5 by 15 cm is the ideal size.
Glue two layers together and it will last far longer.
Round off the corners, they survive much better inside a book.

challenges.title: A second life
challenges.description: Turn something headed for the trash into a small decoration.
tips: Look in your bin or recycling first, the idea will come from there.
A repurposed object doesn't need to be useful, just nice to look at.
Jars, tins and corks are the easiest things to repurpose.

challenges.title: Mini collage
challenges.description: Make a small collage from paper scraps or old magazines.
tips: Cut out a good ten pieces before you start gluing anything.
Lay it all out unglued first, move things around, then fix them.
Postcard size is plenty, no need to go big.

challenges.title: Origami crane
challenges.description: Fold a paper crane, the classic origami symbol. A tutorial is fine if you need one.
tips: Use a perfect square, the crane doesn't forgive a crooked sheet.
The bird base is the hard step, do it twice if you need to.
A failed first crane is a rite of passage, the second one goes better.

challenges.title: Improvised card
challenges.description: Make a spur-of-the-moment greeting card for someone, using whatever's on hand.
tips: Fold your sheet in half: the card already exists, now just decorate it.
Write the message before decorating, you'll manage the space better.
A simple repeated pattern beats one big failed drawing.

challenges.title: Mini herbarium
challenges.description: Pick up a leaf or flower outside and start a mini herbarium.
tips: Pick flat leaves, they dry far better.
Slide them between two sheets of paper inside a heavy book.
Note the date and place, that's what gives a herbarium its charm.

challenges.title: Box makeover
challenges.description: Decorate a box, jar, or pot you were about to throw away.
tips: Clean and dry the surface properly, otherwise nothing sticks.
Glued paper covers faster and more cleanly than paint.
One dominant colour gives a much tidier result.

challenges.title: Improvised bracelet
challenges.description: Make a bracelet or keychain with whatever's on hand.
tips: Measure your wrist with a piece of string before cutting.
Three braided strands are enough for something sturdy.
Thread, shoelace, ribbon, an old cut-up t-shirt: anything works.

challenges.title: Paper garland
challenges.description: Fold and cut out a simple paper garland.
tips: Fold your sheet accordion-style before cutting, that's the whole trick.
Never cut through the two outer folds or everything falls apart.
Simple shapes repeat much better than complicated ones.
